correctness.rationale: The exact compactness norm follows from the adjoint monomial formula and an evaluated Gaussian integral. Taylor expansion at the unique affine fixed point determines all nonzero eigenvalues, proves simplicity, and determines Riesz projections. Gaussian moments and the derivative reproducing kernel yield both dual vector norms and the exact Laguerre identity. A direct ratio-concentration proof for the positive Bessel series plus Laplace integral yields the sharp fixed-displacement prefactor; dominated convergence gives the varying-displacement crossover; uniform boundedness of coordinate rank-one projections forces failure of any Schauder ordering and normal/spectral-type similarity. The standalone script verified 993 supplementary finite identities and numerics, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A standard non-weighted compact affine Fock composition family has spectrum and simple eigenvalues independent of displacement but arbitrarily badly conditioned Riesz projections as n grows. The exact Laguerre formula, its sharp exponential-in-square-root index with prefactor, and the nontrivial Bessel crossover at critical displacement establish a structural spectral-conditioning boundary, with meaningful basis and similarity consequences. This mathematical distinction is not supplied by known eigenvalues or compactness and is not a table computation or arbitrary parameter slice.
